topic: Observable two-wave diagnostic for Palm population variance under exact finite-range local interference. Under bounded local exposure outcomes and two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves sharing one no-carryover schedule, identify Ω_pop by cross-wave IPW moments; prove uniform finite-sample concentration, size and power, an exactly unbiased lag-separated diagnostic, and a sharp root-n score-vector minimax rate at balanced assignment. Janson’s coboundary result is cited substrate. No ANI transfer, endogenous graph-distance HAC, annealed CLT/Wald theorem, or Bond-et-al. reanalysis is claimed.

open_problems.open_problem: Does Leung's unchanged sample-mean-centered graph-HAC estimator consistently estimate the full annealed variance of an exposure-IPW estimator on one stationary ergodic, exponentially stabilizing sparse random network, with asymptotically orthogonal assignment and Palm-population components?

source_refs.claim: Leung proves exposure-IPW asymptotic normality under ANI on a fixed finite population and interprets the graph-HAC remainder as heterogeneity bias relative to assignment variance.
source_refs.author: Michael P. Leung

source_refs.claim: The paper separates design and sampling uncertainty and shows that the corresponding variance formulas need not coincide.
source_refs.author: Alberto Abadie, Susan Athey, Guido W. Imbens, and Jeffrey M. Wooldridge

source_refs.excerpt: The proposal studies finite-population Horvitz--Thompson exposure contrasts in ego-cluster experiments
The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target.
the substantive projection/covariance objects and convergence/strict-separation properties placed into assumptions

open_problems.why_unsolved: Leung conditions on fixed potential outcomes and a fixed graph, so his heterogeneous-effect remainder is a bias relative to assignment variance rather than a population-fluctuation term. The prior ego-cluster and graphon proposals likewise stop at fixed-potential or realized finite-population targets, and the failed ANI comparison was rejected because covariance convergence was assumed instead of derived. A resolution must split the score into an assignment-centered coordinate and a graph-conditional mean, prove a stable conditional CLT jointly with a stabilizing-field CLT, and show that Leung's HAC expansion recovers the resulting Palm covariance rather than merely bounding a fixed-network remainder.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint quenched-annealed stable-CLT theorem with independent Gaussian assignment and environment coordinates, an explicit Ω_ann = Ω_des + Ω_pop formula, and consistency of unchanged graph HAC with its remainder R_n converging to Ω_pop.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from ANI to exposure-IPW and feasible graph-HAC inference is the closest motivation arc, with population uncertainty added as the unresolved step.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact neighborhood interference is brittle -> ANI permits decaying distant effects -> exposure-IPW admits graph-HAC inference on a fixed network -> one random network requires Palm-centered annealed inference and a full variance decomposition

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the ANI score localization, dependency-neighborhood normal approximation, and sample-centered graph-HAC expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact estimator and HAC algebra whose conditional remainder must become the random-network population variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Use physical-dependence projections for iid-innovation random fields, finite-radius approximation, and sample-autocovariance convergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A translation-equivariant local-innovation graph and its Palm score form a Bernoulli-shift field, matching the required population-score CLT and covariance series.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent the statistic as a sum of stabilizing local scores and identify the Gaussian covariance through Palm and add-one calculations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired Ω_pop is the long-run covariance of a translation-equivariant stabilizing score on a random graph.

open_problems.open_problem: Which primitive conditions make a sample-centered cutoff quadratic indexed by an endogenous graph distance converge to the full Palm long-run variance when both scores and distance are generated by the same stabilizing innovations, and when does a persistent distance-selection term invalidate graph HAC?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves network-HAC consistency under tradeoffs among network-shell growth, bandwidth, and decay of network dependence.
source_refs.author: Denis Kojevnikov, Vadim Marmer, and Kyungchul Song

source_refs.claim: The paper proves spatial-HAC consistency when one or several distance measures may be measured with error.
source_refs.author: Harry H. Kelejian and Ingmar R. Prucha

source_refs.excerpt: The boundary cases to compute explicitly are a three-block graph with one cross-block leakage edge
Work out one nondegenerate boundary example where Delta_eta is zero
The substantive econometric content ... was uniformly shifted into Assumptions 5/7/8/9 rather than proved

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing network-HAC proofs index dependence by observed graph distance, and spatial-HAC robustness allows distance measurement error, but neither treats the cutoff 1{d_G(i,j)≤b_n} as a nonlinear selector generated by the same innovations as both scores. Metric compatibility controls large-scale comparison but need not eliminate a four-root selection covariance involving two score roots and the innovations determining a shortest path. The prior ANI run's central defect was assuming precisely such covariance convergence. Searches for endogenous-random-metric HAC found no theorem covering this coupling, so the early kill test must either prove selection neutrality or exhibit a legal stabilizing local-chord counterexample.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem with explicit four-root covariance, random-ball boundary, and sample-centering bounds, paired with a stationary connected exponentially stabilizing counterexample showing nonzero graph-HAC bias when those conditions fail while spatial-distance HAC remains consistent.

writing_exemplar.why: Its dependence-decay versus shell-growth framing is the natural setup, with endogenous metric selection isolated as the missing obstacle.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Network dependence is indexed by graph distance -> graph HAC truncates covariance shells -> shell growth and dependence decay control ordinary truncation -> shared innovations make the cutoff itself selective and require a new quadratic lemma or counterexample

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose HAC error into covariance-tail bias, stochastic shell error, and centering error, then strengthen every term for a random cutoff correlated with both factors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result concerns the same cutoff quadratic, with endogenous metric selection as the sole new dependence channel.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace innovation functionals by finite-radius projections and prove covariance and sample-autocovariance convergence using physical-dependence summability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite-radius projection exposes the four innovation roots governing a score pair and its random shortest-path event.

method_exemplars.technique: Use ambient-distance kernel truncation as a comparator whose indexing metric is not changed by local random chords.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It makes the proposed spatial-HAC pivot mathematically testable on exactly the same stabilized score field.

open_problems.open_problem: Can annealed graph-HAC validity be strengthened to uniform Wald coverage over a nondegenerate class of stabilizing graph rules, ANI decay sequences, exposure probabilities, and admissible data-dependent graph-distance bandwidths?

source_refs.claim: The paper shows network-HAC covariance estimates can be anti-conservative under interference and proposes a positive-semidefinite conservative modification.
source_refs.author: Mengsi Gao and Peng Ding

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains explicit normal-approximation rates for sums of exponentially stabilizing local scores.
source_refs.author: Mathew D. Penrose and J. E. Yukich

source_refs.excerpt: If the variance OEQ succeeds, add a feasible Wald theorem using Vbar_n
The observable envelope replaces the schedule-specific design variance and can be conservative

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pointwise CLT plus pointwise variance consistency does not imply uniform coverage when the graph rule, ANI tail, bandwidth, positivity constant, and variance approach admissibility boundaries together. Prior interference proposals obtained fixed-graph or conservative intervals and explicitly deferred feasible exact Wald inference; Gao and Ding show that studentization can under-cover even when point estimation is asymptotically normal. The missing work couples quantitative stabilization-based Gaussian approximation with uniform exact-HAC ratio consistency and an admissible bandwidth selector, while excluding total-variance degeneracy.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform Berry-Esseen and graph-HAC ratio-consistency theorem yielding sup_P |P_P{τ_Palm(P)∈CI_n}-(1-α)|→0, with a feasible bandwidth selector and explicit positivity and lower-variance boundaries.

writing_exemplar.why: Its arc from familiar HAC practice to concrete undercoverage and a coverage-facing repair is the best model for stating why uniform validity matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Network experiments invite familiar robust-SE workflows -> graph HAC can be anti-conservative -> asymptotic validity must be expressed as coverage -> identify a stabilizing class where the unchanged annealed studentizer is uniformly exact

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Stein's method to exponentially stabilizing score sums using stabilization-radius tails and local moment envelopes to obtain uniform Kolmogorov rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform Wald coverage requires a quantitative parameter-uniform CLT for locally determined score sums.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand spatial-HAC bias and variance, optimize truncated MSE, and prove consistency of a plug-in bandwidth.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same bias-variance program can yield a feasible graph-distance bandwidth after deterministic pair counts are replaced by uniform random-shell bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain the ANI truncation, graph-HAC studentization, and heterogeneous-effect remainder decomposition while making every remainder class-uniform.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed interval deliberately keeps Leung's estimator and studentizer unchanged.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the correct studentized limit and feasible inference procedure for exposure-IPW effects on a stationary but nonergodic stabilizing network when an invariant common shock makes the population variance random?

source_refs.claim: Without ergodicity, Dedecker's stationary-random-field CLT yields a Gaussian mixture whose scale is measurable with respect to the invariant sigma-field.
source_refs.author: Jérôme Dedecker

source_refs.claim: The review emphasizes that fixed- and random-network frameworks differ in generalizability when expected outcomes change with network structure.
source_refs.author: Subhankar Bhadra and Michael Schweinberger

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ergodicity turns the Palm covariance series into a constant estimable from one expanding realization; a common invariant shock instead produces an order-one latent component or random long-run variance. Dedecker supplies a mixed-Gaussian random-field limit but not an exposure-IPW score with independent Bernoulli assignment, while causal variance decompositions do not determine what one network reveals about the invariant component. Unchanged HAC may therefore estimate only a conditional random scale and miss unconditional common-shock uncertainty.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A regime theorem giving the mixed-normal or inconsistent limit under an invariant common shock, a characterization of the conditional scale estimated by graph HAC, and either a feasible self-normalized confidence procedure or an impossibility theorem for unconditional Palm-effect coverage from one network.

writing_exemplar.why: Its emphasis on graph-to-graph variation provides the right causal interpretation of the invariant-shock boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Random outcomes and graphs broaden the target beyond one fixed network -> one realization supports population inference through ergodicity -> an invariant common shock survives network growth -> characterize the mixed limit and what coverage remains possible

method_exemplars.technique: Use projective approximation and a Lindeberg argument conditional on the invariant sigma-field to obtain a Gaussian mixture with random variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired failure boundary is exactly a stationary nonergodic random-field limit with invariant-measurable scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on outcomes and graph, localize assignment dependence under ANI, and retain the graph-HAC expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditional assignment fluctuations still follow Leung's machinery even when the environment component is nonergodic.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one characterize exactly when the Palm-population component Ω_pop of an annealed exposure-IPW limit is zero, positive, or lower order, and derive the alternate normalization and limit at the homogeneous or dense degeneracy boundary?

source_refs.claim: Under graphon random-graph asymptotics, direct-effect estimators retain a root-n CLT in dense regimes and can be first-order assignment-driven.
source_refs.author: Shuangning Li and Stefan Wager

source_refs.claim: The paper provides an explicit nondegeneracy criterion for limiting variances of stabilizing geometric functionals.
source_refs.author: Peter Eichelsbacher, Martin Raič, and Tomasz Schreiber
source_refs.venue: Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré, Probabilités et Statistiques

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dense-network causal CLTs can become assignment-dominated, while stabilizing-functional CLTs usually assume or separately verify positive linear-order variance. Neither literature characterizes Ω_pop for exposure-conditioned causal scores as a property of outcome heterogeneity and the local graph rule. If Ω_des stays positive, ordinary annealed inference can survive Ω_pop=0, but the population coordinate may require another normalization and may have a non-Gaussian second-order limit; no statement-level projection criterion currently pins down that boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient projection or add-one-cost criterion for Ω_pop=0, a usable sufficient condition for Ω_pop>0, and a second-order normalization-and-limit theorem for the degenerate population score.

writing_exemplar.why: Its density-regime narrative shows how network asymptotics change which uncertainty component survives and naturally motivates a variance phase boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference creates dependent estimator errors -> network density changes which fluctuations survive -> direct-effect estimation may become assignment-dominated -> characterize exactly when population fluctuation vanishes and what replaces it

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze local add-one perturbations and cluster cumulants to certify positive linear-order variance for stabilizing sums.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Ω_pop is the limiting variance of a stabilizing Palm score, so add-one nondegeneracy directly separates zero from positive variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Identify covariance functionals of stabilizing random measures and derive multivariate Gaussian limits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its Palm covariance representation can expose the precise projection whose cancellation makes Ω_pop vanish.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand direct-effect estimators under graphon asymptotics and isolate assignment-driven leading terms across density regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested dense/homogeneous boundary asks for an analogous leading-term classification under local stabilizing graph generation.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what empirically checkable local-stabilization and network-growth conditions can the Bond et al. 61-million-user Facebook experiment be reanalyzed for a Palm population exposure effect with standard errors including assignment and network-population variation?

source_refs.claim: The experiment randomized political-mobilization messages to 61 million Facebook users and reported effects on users, friends, and friends of friends.
source_refs.author: Robert M. Bond, Christopher J. Fariss, Jason J. Jones, Adam D. I. Kramer, Cameron Marlow, Jaime E. Settle, and James H. Fowler

source_refs.claim: The paper gives exposure-mapping IPW estimators, randomization-based variance estimators, and local-dependence asymptotic normality for social-network experiments.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow and Cyrus Samii

source_refs.claim: The review states that fixed- and random-network frameworks differ in generalizability because expected outcomes can change with network structure.
source_refs.author: Subhankar Bhadra and Michael Schweinberger

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bond et al. establish randomized social transmission on one realized platform network, but a population interpretation is broader than that exact Election Day graph. Existing exposure-mapping analyses are assignment-based, while random-network work stresses graph-to-graph generalizability. The first changed proof step is not IPW algebra but verification that the Facebook user/network sequence has a translation-equivariant or locally weak Palm limit and stabilizing exposure outcomes; without that correspondence, Ω_pop is not identified by the proposed asymptotics.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A correspondence theorem and diagnostic protocol mapping the Facebook experiment to a locally convergent stabilizing-network model, followed by a Palm-effect IPW estimator, a joint assignment/population CLT, and a reported variance decomposition or a formal rejection of the model when diagnostics fail.

writing_exemplar.why: Its direct-to-social-transmission motivation and immense single-network design provide the destination framing without implying that it posed the annealed-inference problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Online messages may change offline political behavior -> randomization identifies direct and social transmission effects on the realized Facebook network -> broader population claims require graph-to-graph uncertainty -> reanalyze the exposure effect around a Palm target with annealed standard errors

method_exemplars.technique: Compute exposure probabilities from the randomized design, form Horvitz-Thompson exposure contrasts, and use local-dependence variance and normal-approximation arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the design-based point estimator and assignment component for a social-network experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace exact exposure sufficiency by ANI decay, localize distant-assignment effects, and estimate dependence with graph-distance HAC.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Friends-of-friends transmission makes approximate rather than exact neighborhood interference the relevant bridge to a feasible estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose regression uncertainty into design-based and sampling-based components and state conditions under which standard errors include both.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The reanalysis must separate Facebook treatment-randomization uncertainty from treating the realized network as one draw from a target population.

literature_map:
Leung (2022, Econometrica, arXiv:1911.07085) is the exact ANI anchor: exposure-IPW asymptotic normality plus a sample-centered network-HAC whose finite-population bias is the variance of unit-level exposure effects.
Gao and Ding (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2309.07476) show that network-HAC can be anti-conservative under interference and propose a positive-semidefinite conservative modification.
Kojevnikov, Marmer, and Song (2021, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1903.01059) give general network LLN/CLT/HAC theory based on dependence decay, shell growth, and logarithmic bandwidths.
Kojevnikov (2021, arXiv:2101.12312) supplies block and dependent-wild-bootstrap alternatives for network-dependent means, but not annealed causal scores on an endogenous random metric.
Li and Wager (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2007.13302) develop graphon random-graph causal asymptotics; they obtain direct-effect CLTs but describe the asymptotic variance as difficult to estimate.
Park and Wager (2026, arXiv:2603.25032) extend direct-effect CLTs to convergent dense nonrandom graphs and find first-order assignment-dominated uncertainty.
Bhadra and Schweinberger (2026, arXiv:2508.06808) contrast fixed- and random-network causal frameworks and identify graph-dependent generalizability as an open concern.
Abadie, Athey, Imbens, and Wooldridge (2020, Econometrica, arXiv:1706.01778) provide the closest econometric template for separating design and population uncertainty.
El Machkouri, Volný, and Wu (2013, SPA, arXiv:1109.0838) prove CLTs and sample-autocovariance limits for iid-innovation stationary ergodic random fields via physical dependence.
Baryshnikov and Yukich (2005, Annals of Applied Probability, arXiv:math/0503474) provide stabilizing-score Gaussian limits and Palm covariance functionals for random geometric measures.
Penrose and Yukich (2005, arXiv:math/0409088) and Eichelsbacher, Raič, and Schreiber (2015, arXiv:1010.1665) add quantitative normal approximation and variance-nondegeneracy tools.
Kelejian and Prucha (2007) and Kim and Sun (2011), both in Journal of Econometrics, cover spatial-HAC distance error and plug-in bandwidths, but not a cutoff metric endogenously generated with the scores.
Dedecker (1998, PTRF) shows that dropping ergodicity naturally yields invariant-sigma-field Gaussian mixtures, supplying the common-shock failure boundary.
Aronow and Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics, arXiv:1305.6156) and Sävje, Aronow, and Hudgens (2021, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1711.06399) anchor exposure-IPW and unknown-interference design-based asymptotics.
Bond et al. (2012, Nature, DOI:10.1038/nature11421) is the motivating 61-million-user single-network experiment; the scan found no published Palm-population/HAC reanalysis incorporating random-network variation.
prior_proposal_map:
A bounded scan of active and banked CausalSmith research found no prior proposal whose theorem target is explicitly annealed, quenched, or Palm-centered; those terms occur only in the current run state.
The closest prior qid is failed panel_approx_nbhd_interference/v1; its proposal models ANI exposure-IPW and graph HAC, while its D0.5 review says the substantive covariance convergence was assumed rather than proved.
Its angle0_v4 reviewer JSON also requested nondegenerate boundary examples, directly supporting the endogenous-random-metric kill-test direction.
Downgraded exp_ego_cluster_exposure_clt/ego_cluster_polynomial_clt supplies a sound fixed-potential exposure-HT dependency-graph CLT and feasible-Wald substrate, but no environment fluctuation.
Downgraded exp_graphon_indirect_honest_length_frontier/v1 treats one random graph and Bernoulli assignment but explicitly keeps a realized finite-population target and graph-conditional certification.
Downgraded exp_interference_nonasymp_effcount/holder_fractional_coloring_bernstein_eprocess supplies finite-sample design-based coverage machinery while admitting that its observable variance envelope is conservative.
No relevant archived angle-rejected proposal supplied a closer Palm-population or exact annealed-HAC kernel.
